exposure: tined lead test phase for sacral neuromodulation (SNM)
previous transurethral resection of the prostate and/or bladder neck incision
inability to void during a urodynamic study
outcome: success rate of tined lead test phase (>=50% reduction of clean intermittent catheterization frequency or postvoid residual)
long-term treatment efficacy (continued use of SNM system)
cohort: This study included 215 consecutive patients (82 men and 133 women) who underwent a tined lead test phase for the treatment of nonobstructive urinary retention (NOUR).
finding: The success rate of the tined lead test phase for nonobstructive urinary retention was significantly higher in women (62%) than in men (22%), with age and history of psychiatric illness predicting success in women, and age and previous transurethral resection of the prostate/bladder neck incision predicting success in men.
